[title] Survey Results Summary statistics Quantiles and boxplots Python/Colab Outlook Example 7: Ultimate shear strength of steel fillet welds
[body] The ultimate shear strength of a material is its maximum allowable force per unit area prior to sliding failure. This is measured for a sample of fillet welds:
[body] The sample size is 41. The sample mean is 56.4 ksi. The standard deviation is 6.2 ksi. Note: the mean and standard deviation have the same units
[body] Prof. Oke (UMass Amherst) CEE 260/MIE 273 M1b: Summarizing Data September 10, 2026 7 / 16

FIGURE: [description of the image, not printed words] A histogram has a horizontal axis labelled “Ultimate shear strength, ksi” with ticks at 10, 50, 60, and 70, and a vertical axis labelled “Frequency, percent” with ticks at 0, 10, 20, and 30. Outlined bars span roughly 42–75 ksi, with the tallest near 54–57 ksi; a small isolated bar appears near 72–75 ksi. Beside it: “n = 41”, “x̄ = 56.4”, and “s = 6.2”. At upper right, a small labelled “Fillet Welds” drawing has four weld cross-sections labelled “mitre”, “multiple”, “convex”, and “concave”.
